title: Webers and Maxwells: Magnetic Flux Units
h1: Webers and maxwells — the flux linking a coil
description: The weber is the SI unit of magnetic flux. The maxwell is its CGS ancestor, 10⁸ times smaller. Here is where each still appears.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

hero: 1 Wb = 10⁸ Mx. The weber is enormous; magnetic circuits routinely deal in microwebers. Transformer cores are sized around it.
body: Magnetic flux Φ is the integral of magnetic field over an area. It shows up in every electromagnetic induction problem: Faraday's law relates the rate of change of flux to an induced EMF. The unit choice (Wb vs Mx) depends on whether the paper is SI or CGS.

> 1 Wb = 1 V·s (definition via Faraday)
> 1 Wb = 10⁸ Mx (maxwell, CGS)
> 1 Mx = 10⁻⁸ Wb
> 1 Wb/m² = 1 T (tesla, flux density)
> Small transformer core flux: 1–10 mWb

EMF (volts) = −dΦ/dt (webers per second). A 1 V generator produces 1 weber of flux change per second in a single-turn coil. Multi-turn coils multiply the EMF: N turns × dΦ/dt gives total EMF. Every transformer, motor and generator design starts with this equation.

A 50 Hz transformer core operating at peak flux density B̂ (typically 1.5–1.7 T for silicon steel) with core cross-section A has peak flux Φ̂ = B̂ × A. Volts per turn = 4.44 × f × Φ̂. A 230 V primary at 50 Hz needing 2 V/turn requires 115 turns. Core cross-section for 1.5 T peak: A = 2 / (4.44 × 50 × 1.5) = 6 × 10⁻³ m² = 60 cm² — a modest transformer.

Legacy magnetics textbooks, old motor rewinding notes, and CGS-tradition physics papers. Modern engineering uses webers exclusively. Both units survive together in graduate physics because CGS formulations of Maxwell's equations are cleaner (no 4π factors) than SI.
1 Wb = 1 V·s = 10⁸ Mx. Faraday: EMF = N × dΦ/dt. Transformer volts/turn = 4.44 × f × Φ̂. Cores sized by cross-section and peak flux density.

faqs.q: How is flux different from flux density?
faqs.a: Flux Φ (Wb) is total; flux density B (T) is per unit area. B = Φ / A. A larger area at the same B has more total flux.
4.44 = 2π/√2 — from the RMS-to-peak conversion of a sinusoidal EMF.
Yes — flux is a signed quantity, direction defined by the surface normal. Sign flips give the negative in Faraday's law.
